title: How Milt Hinton came into Cab's band in Chicago
summary: Hinton recalls Cab hearing him at the Three Deuces on Keg Johnson's recommendation after bassist Al Morgan stayed in California.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So now it's 1936, and we're in the Cotton Club downtown.
Well, that's when we come in town... We came in town that time with our best band.
Well, that's where I came in. I came in the band then.
Yeah, because we got, we picked up...
You picked me up in Chicago.
And where did Bass... Did Bass leave us? How did we happen to pick you up?
Bass left you in California after you did The Singing Kid with Al Jolson. Al Morgan stayed out there.
He stayed out there. And you were coming through Chicago, coming back East...
Yeah, and we needed a bass player.

Keg Johnson, who was a dear friend of mine, recommended me, and sent Cab down to hear me at the Three Deuces. Then Cab came and heard me with Zuttie Singleton and Art Tatum and Lee Collins and Eddie Barksdale...
And he hired me on the spot...until he could get to New York and get a good bass player. And the rest of the story is my story.
He didn't know he had a good bass player. He didn't know.
But it was thanks to you and Lamar Wright... And you can tell the story about the first trip I made on the road, and I didn't know where to go to stay -- there was no places for us to stay.
